notes.title: Devlog: The Sewer Tunnel
notes.content:
[h1][b]THE SEWER TUNNEL[/b][/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43682030/688235b3ac724b4b965a6a234bf1507cf2a7cc0d.gif[/img]

The second level of the game, The Grand Ocean, is a water-based level with multiple areas and transitions where the core gameplay revolves around movement challenges.

After defeating the boss in level one, Soraya and the Little One find themselves traveling through sewer tunnels full of sludge and pollution, hoping that "all rivers lead to the sea". It's dark and dank in the tunnel and all the enemies are based off of bugs and amphibians: gnats, horned-toads, and [i]dragonflies...[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43682030/f6b9626c4b6d6c730a42997d018afd1297a20c84.gif[/img]

If you don't know how to use the dash effectively yet, you will when you face the horned-toad!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43682030/a35ca2a5dc86d30cbd4984102a310747081b0788.gif[/img]

The. next area of the game is a canyon that leads to the titular Grand Ocean. More soon.

Best,
Austin

notes.title: Demo Update 1.3.1
notes.content:
Hi all - Austin here!

Holidays are over and it's time to get back to work with what should be (fingers crossed ːsteamhappyː) the final main update to the demo.

The two main issues I kept seeing about the demo were that the intro tutorial and the intended strategy for the demo boss were too unclear.

[h1]Streamlined Tutorial[/h1]
You might think tutorials are easy to make, but there are so many kinds of players at different skill and literacy levels that it's really hard to make something that works for everyone. It's REALLY hard to figure what to tell the player, how much, and at what speed. For example, the tutorial currently only has three parts and it covers shooting, comboing, combo+, and rewinding time. But there are a lot more mechanics in the game! For example, Dashing, Dashing + Absorbing time bullets at the same time, Point-Blank damage increase, bonuses when large enemies fall into smaller ones, rewind penalties, and [i]more[/i] are not explained in the initial tutorial.

I have always been inspired by Hyper Light Drifter and how that game used next-to-nothing in terms of text. That's why the "How to Play" section had the images of what you were supposed to do instead of words. But that was a little too cryptic. So now they take away the controls for a moment to just display the image and words explaining what it means:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43682030/744b945fcd720462b921f5a6cbeff1199b45024e.gif[/img]

Much cleaner!

[h1]The Self-Coordination Problem[/h1]
The demo's boss has one main purpose: to skill gate player's who can coordinate with their future/past selves. The intended way to defeat the boss is to open up one of the four joints inn one timeline, then rewind and shoot the opened joint in another. But MOST PEOPLE WEREN'T DOING THAT!

The main reason why, I think, wasn't actually about telegraphing what to do - this fix addresses that too - but that it was much too easy to unintentionally open [i]and[/i] attack the joints at the same time.

So to address that, I adjusted both the hitbox of the joint and the way the covers retract so that it's MUCH harder to do that. And to really drive the point home I added this quick tip at the beginning of the fight:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43682030/b06ee27786ee9c62579ceb160ea1aabf2813a46e.gif[/img]

[h1]Patch List[/h1]
[h2]Tweaks and Features:[/h2]
[list]
[*] "How to Play" tutorials clearer and more explicit text.
[*] Added mini tutorial animation when starting Demo Boss (Lewha).
[*] Demo Boss (Lewha) joints hitbox adjusted.
[*] Better fonts for Main Menu text and messaging.
[*] Fullscreen on startup.
[*] "Backpack" enemy goes to initial bullet sweep faster.
[*] "How to Play" Combo/Combo+ tutorials number of times to succeed adjusted.
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]MAJOR FIX[/b]: Enemies no longer duplicate when rewind ends on same frame as when enemy is created.
[*] Alt-Enter will toggle fullscreen without skipping tutorial if "SKIP" is available.
[/list]

notes.title: Devlog: Ramping Up Development in 2025
notes.content:
Merry Christmas, Happy Holidays, and Happy New Year!

[h1]Playing some games...[/h1]
At the end of each year I take some time to play a bunch of games. With a full-time job and a family, I spend more time developing games than making them. So I usually grab a couple games during the holiday sales or set aside time to play ones I've been looking forward too. Here's some of the games I've been playing this past month:
[olist]
[*] Ni no Kuni: Wrath of the White Witch (Finishing after bouncing off)
[*] Final Fantasy XII: The Zodiac Age
[*] Hogwarts Legacy
[/olist]

And one more game I've been looking forward to for years and finally made time to play it: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1805240/Layer_Section__Galactic_Attack_STribute/]Layer Section[/url]. This might surprise you but [b]I don't play very many shoot 'em ups![/b] I find most shoot 'em ups to be very derivative, but this is one of those super unique ones and it's super approachable. The push and pull of focusing on surviving in the foreground while locking on to enemies in the background is really fun and frantic. It's definitely worth a look.

[h1]Beaming Stingray in 2025[/h1]
Now that I've had some time off from development, it's time to get back to work. I can't wait to build the remaining levels and mechanics in this game and this break has rekindled the fire to get this thing done. Here are some things I'll be working on starting in the new year:

[list]
[*] New demo with better tutorials and boss tweaks
[*] Grand Ocean sequencing + racing section
[*] Zahar Desert enemy design and 'dungeon' generation
[*] MORE MUSIC
[/list]

I'm trying to make something super unique in the shoot 'em up space with mechanics and enemy design no one's even thought [i]could or should[/i] be in a shoot 'em up.

Can't wait to get to work!
-Austin

notes.title: STEAM NEXT FEST DEMO IS LIVE!
notes.content:
Hey all,

Austin here. The Steam Next Fest demo is now live on the main page. In this demo you'll have a quick tutorial, an intro level, and the [b]full first level of the game[/b] (as it stands now - subject to change!). 

Reminders:
[list]
[*] Pause at (almost) anytime with Esc or the Start button on a controller (or your controller's equivalent).
[*] Toggle fullscreen with Alt-Enter
[*] Cutscenes should become skippable after you've seen them one time (I worked so hard on them you GET to watch them lol)
[/list]

I'm so excited to see how people react to a shoot 'em up that tries to do something different. Send me your high scores!

Enjoy!

notes.title: OFFICIAL ANNOUNCEMENT! It's really real!
notes.content:
WELCOME!

I am Austin Dixon and I am the solo dev behind Beaming Stingray. Today the game was officially announced with the [url=https://youtu.be/8R08Z3XnprY?si=zSoG1xcFrg7JUAxG]Announcement Trailer [/url]on [url=https://twitter.com/austinadixon/status/1841215679476711598]Twitter[/url]!

[previewyoutube=8R08Z3XnprY;rightthumb][/previewyoutube]

Beaming Stingray is the result of 3 years of very VERY long nights and weekends. It all started in November 2021 when, in the span of 40 days, both of my mother's parents passed away. With COVID, other illnesses, and age, these two grandparents were the 6th and 7th recent deaths in my life.

With so much death so close in time, I really started to think about my time on this planet! How long do I have left. Working on this game has been a way for me to process that - all the fear, the anger, the helplessness, and the hope.

Maybe a little deep for a shoot 'em up! But one I hope you'll enjoy when the game releases.

- Austin
